en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Insurance Maps of the New Jersey Coast, Volume One, 1907, Fair Haven, Monmouth County, New Jersey, Sheet 77
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Insurance Maps of the New Jersey Coast, Volume One, 1907, Fair Haven, Monmouth County, New Jersey, Sheet 78, part 1 (main map)

sheet-77.description: This sheet shows the western half of the business centre of Fair Haven, a borough on the south bank of the North Shrewsbury (Navesink) River in Monmouth County, drawn at 60 feet to an inch as sheet 77 of the 1907 New Jersey Coast volume. Main Street, today's River Road, crosses the sheet from left to right a little below the middle, and Pearl Avenue, now Fair Haven Road, runs up the sheet from Willow Avenue at the bottom to the river frontage at the top, where a note reads 'River beyond'. Clay Street runs east from Pearl Avenue to Denormandie, which forms the right edge of the sheet and continues on sheet 78; Avenue A, now Church Street, crosses Main Street at the left edge. North of Main Street west of Pearl Avenue the land is laid out in long, deep lots, several of them angled along a diagonal property line, with scattered frame dwellings, stables and a boat house, and a private lane running west from Pearl Avenue. The blocks east of Pearl Avenue are more closely built with dwellings and outbuildings. The commercial core is at Main Street and Pearl Avenue: a cigar factory, a grocery, the post office, a saloon and hotel, halls, a livery stable marked as burned, the Atlantic Hotel, a parsonage and an ice house. Institutions include the Episcopal church near Avenue A, the M. P. church on Main Street, the fire department house with its hose carriage and hook and ladder truck, and the public school south of Main Street. Water pipes of 18 and 4 inches are drawn in Main Street and along Denormandie, with town hydrants at the corners. The header gives a population of 1200 and notes that water facilities are described in the Long Branch report.
notes: Pearl Avenue is now Fair Haven Road.
Main (Main Street) is now River Road.
Avenue A is now Church Street.
Denormandie is now De Normandie Avenue; Clay is Clay Street and Willow Avenue is Willow Street.
A narrow way west of Pearl Avenue is lettered 'Private'.
The livery stable south of Main Street is marked 'Burned'.
Header: population 1200, prevailing winds west, no steam or hand engine, 500 ft of 2 1/2 inch hose, one independent hose cart, one hook and ladder truck.

Fair Haven (Monmouth County), scale 60 ft to an inch. Pearl Av. (now Fair Haven Road) north and south of Main St. (now River Road), Clay, Willow Av., Avenue A (now Church Street) at the left edge, Denormandie (De Normandie Avenue) at the right edge; one part.

sheet-78-1.description: This part covers the eastern half of Fair Haven's centre on sheet 78 of the 1907 New Jersey Coast volume, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and continuing sheet 77 across Denormandie, which runs along its left edge. Main Street, today's River Road, crosses the lower half of the sheet; Willow Avenue runs along the bottom edge. North of Main Street, Clay Street runs from Denormandie to Normandie Avenue (now the northern end of Gillespie Avenue), which leads up towards the North Shrewsbury River. The river crosses the upper right of the sheet diagonally, and the large waterfront estates between Normandie Avenue and the shore are divided into irregular lots with large dwellings, sheds, a boat house and a boat stand. An unnamed alley runs east parallel to Main Street behind the Main Street lots. South of Main Street, Gillespie (now Oak Place) and Kemp (now Elm Place) run down to Willow Avenue, and a 16 ft street lettered 'Not Named' leaves Main Street near the right edge; a note at the bottom reads 'Kemp St. Row of frame dwgs beyond'. The built-up area is almost entirely frame dwellings with stables and outbuildings; the few other buildings are a blacksmith and wheelwright shop on Main Street, two small shops coloured green like the smithy (one on the alley, one on Gillespie), an ice house near the right edge, and a store at the corner of Denormandie and Main Street. Water pipes of 18 and 4 inches run in Main Street and Denormandie, with town hydrants at the corners. The inset in the upper right, the Rumsen Improvement Ass'n pumping station, is a separate part and is not covered here.
notes: Normandie Avenue (north of Main) lines up with today's Gillespie Avenue north of River Road.
Gillespie (south of Main) is now Oak Place; Kemp is now Elm Place.
Main (Main Street) is now River Road; Denormandie is De Normandie Avenue; Willow Avenue is Willow Street.
A 16 ft street east of Kemp is lettered 'Not Named'.
The North Shrewsbury River is today usually called the Navesink River.

Fair Haven, scale 60 ft to an inch. Denormandie, Normandie Av. (now the north end of Gillespie Avenue), Clay, Main (River Road), Gillespie (now Oak Place), Kemp (now Elm Place), Willow Av., North Shrewsbury River. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 inset of the Rumsen Improvement Ass'n pumping station, 3/4 mile SE of Fair Haven (single works, no streets; unplaced).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Rumsen Improvement Ass'n pumping station, 3/4 mile S.E. of Fair Haven (no street junction; a single works drawn with no streets; needs a hand-picked point on the pumping station building with a known modern location, px_per_ft and north_deg).
